items.title: Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
items.detailText:
Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
The proposed offering consists of 825,000,000 shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 801,351,354 shares are being offered by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders. Anthropic will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders. Anthropic also expects to grant the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares of its Class A common stock.
The initial public offering price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share. Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.”
The proposed offering will be made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the preliminary prospectus may be obtained from: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, NY 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10014.
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation. Our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

items.title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
items.detailText:
Today, we’re excited to introduce Muse Spark 1.1, the latest model from Meta Superintelligence Labs and a significant upgrade from Muse Spark. Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with major gains in tool and computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding.
With these improvements, Muse Spark 1.1 advances the performance-efficiency frontier. Together with this week’s launch of Muse Image , this release brings us closer to our vision of personal superintelligence: models that help you pursue your goals, create what you imagine, deepen your relationships, and take action on what you value most.
Along with this release, we are launching a public preview of the new Meta Model API where developers can access Muse Spark 1.1. The model is available now in "Thinking" mode in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai .
For more details about our evaluations, see our report .
Muse Spark 1.1 delivers exceptional performance in personal agentic tasks that require planning and orchestration across a range of external apps and services. It zero-shot generalizes to new native tools, MCP servers, and custom skills.
It tackles complex projects significantly faster than Muse Spark, as it is trained to orchestrate multi-agent systems to optimize end-to-end latency. As the main agent, it can gather context, make a plan, and delegate execution across parallel subagents. As a subagent, it adheres to its job, understands available tools, and knows when to escalate back to the main agent.
Muse Spark 1.1 can actively manage its context window of 1 million tokens. It remembers actions, retrieves information from much earlier work, and compacts in a way that keeps the critical steps needed for later work.
Muse Spark 1.1 excels at computer-use workflows that unfold across multiple applications with information changing on-the-fly. It maintains context across extended sessions, adapts to evolving requirements, and navigates unfamiliar interfaces with minimal human intervention.
Rather than reasoning through every desktop step one click at a time, Muse Spark 1.1 understands when to automate and when to use the interface directly. We trained the model to write scripts when automation is faster, click when direct interaction is simpler, and generate batches of actions at each step.
Agentic dinner party organization: In real-world applications, new context arises that changes the task. Muse Spark 1.1 notices these changes when placing the dinner order and makes necessary updates without user intervention.

items.title: Introducing Muse Image and Muse Video
items.detailText:
Muse Image follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, composes from multiple references, and draws on Instagram for social context. Muse...
We’re excited to launch Muse Image and preview Muse Video, the first media generation models developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Image is our most advanced image generation model yet: it follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, and composes from multiple references. It also brings agentic tool use capabilities and integrates with Muse Spark. Muse Video, built on the same pretraining base, delivers exceptional visual fidelity with native audio support.
Muse Image is available today across the Meta AI app and on meta.ai , Instagram Stories in the US, and WhatsApp in limited countries, and is coming soon to Facebook. Muse Video is coming soon to creators and Meta AI.
Instead of directly mapping prompts to images, Muse Image operates as an agent: it invokes search and coding tools to improve accuracy, self-refines its own generations, and improves through scaling test-time compute. Muse Image also integrates with Muse Spark, allowing the two models to share tools and plan jointly for powerful agentic media generation.
We provide Muse Image with access to tools to enhance its agentic capabilities.
Coding. During reinforcement learning, Muse Image learns to write and execute code that produces accurate plots and QR codes, and condition on rendered figures to improve the accuracy of generated images. Muse Spark and Muse Image also integrate to use the combination of code and media generation to create animated GIFs, websites with embedded images, and interactive visual games.
Search. Muse Image learns to search the web to ground generated images in factual and real-time information and visual references. Enabling search improves factual accuracy on knowledge-intensive prompts, particularly those involving current events and real-world facts.
Muse Image improves with search tool use. Win rate from internal ablation.
Muse Image reflects on and improves upon its own work within its chain of thought. This self-refining behavior can take different forms: a local edit to the current image draft when a small detail is off, a new image generation from scratch when larger parts are wrong, or a different tactic like tool use for more factually accurate generation. We didn’t design this behavior. Instead, it emerged during RL training simply because self-refinement produced better images and therefore higher reward.
Muse Image improves with emergent self-refinement. Win rate from internal ablation.
Muse Image improves with scaling test-time compute. Elo from internal ablation.
Muse Image edits images with precision, changing exactly what the user asks for. It can follow a variety of instruction

items.title: AI算力基础设施盈利分化加剧，主体与收入性质决定谁能先盈利
items.detailText:
四类主体的分化不是同一起点上的领先落后，而是四种生意模式的并立。
同样一座智算中心，由地方国资平台出资建设，与由云厂商联合芯片厂共建运营，从立项第一天起就在两本不同的账上：
前者的钱来自财政资金与固定资产投资，收入靠机架出租、政府购买与补贴政策；后者的钱来自经营性现金流，收入跟着自有业务的调用量走，按用量结算。
2026 年，两组数据把这种差异摆到了台面上——国家数据局口径显示，全国在用智算中心已超过 500 个、在建及规划近 400 个，总数接近 1000 个，而行业估算平均利用率仍只有两三成 [7][14] ；与此同时，头部云厂商多次公开披露算力利用率处于高位、服务器资源紧张 [1] 。差异的根源不在技术路线，而在运营主体是谁、钱从哪里来、需求由谁产生。
AI 算力基础设施运营主体已分化为政府主导与国资平台、电信运营商、公有云厂商、第三方算力服务商四类，资源获取方式、需求生成机制与盈利逻辑均不相同；把四类主体放进同一套评价体系，是当前多数智算中心经营判断失真的来源。 接下来的关键，是把「谁在运营」还原为「谁出钱、谁使用、谁受益」，再看资源条件支撑得起什么样的商业模式。
四类主体的分化不是同一起点上的领先落后，而是四种生意模式的并立。 运营商卖的是网络加算力的组合，云厂商卖的是场景加平台的调用，第三方卖的是机房资产加长协服务，国资平台承担的是产业基建职能。评价一座智算中心，先要确认它属于哪一类、按哪一类的逻辑经营，这是后续所有判断的前提。
政府主导与国资平台类主体包括地方政府与地方算力集团、城投产投平台，以及园区开发运营公司。这类主体的核心资源集中在供给端：土地、电力接入、能耗指标、财政专项资金与贴息政策，都优先向智算中心倾斜。公开整理口径显示，2026 年地方算力基建投放约 4000–4500 亿元，与三大运营商约 1420 亿元、同比增长 61.8% 的算力专项投入共同构成投资端的主要盘子[4]；湖北省 2026 年算力券方案统筹 5000 万元、按实际发生费用最高补贴 30%，辽宁按合同额最高补贴 30%、上限 200 万元——补贴落在需求侧，但发钱的仍是地方政府[5][6]。北京、上海、四川、湖北等地已先后通过地方国资平台控股或新设算力中心运营主体，河北建投等能源类国资集团也在以能源主业优势切入算力服务市场[13]。
有资源不等于有需求。土地、能耗指标与财政资金能让智算中心快速建起来，却不能保证建成之后有人来用、用得上量。行业估算全国在用智算中心平均利用率仅 20%–30%，而一座智算中心通常要跨过约四成上架率才能盈亏平衡[7]；采购主体是平台公司，使用方是入驻企业或本地单位，受益方则散落在产业招商目标里，三者常不重合。千卡级的中型项目中，多数国资和西部项目利用率只有 25%–45%、长期亏损[12]。值得注意的是，湖北算力券方案已明确将「所购算力服务非本单位自身使用，存在转让、赠送、买卖、出借」排除在补贴之外，并要求提交合同、付款凭证、使用记录与服务结果[5]——政策层面已经开始甄别采购、使用与受益的分离。
政府主导类主体的价值不在自身盈利，而在产业撬动；但撬动成效要用外部付费与本地应用成效验证，不能用建成规模代替。 对这类主体，上架率、外部付费收入占比与续约情况，比投资额更能说明经营质量。
公有云厂商是四类主体中唯一「场景内生」的一类：自有业务的调用量就是需求本身。2026 年，阿里二季度资本开支 676.8 亿元、同比增长 75%，腾讯同期 527.8 亿元、同比增长 176%，百度 113.9 亿元、同比接近 200%；字节跳动将 2026 年 AI 基础设施支出上调至 2000 亿元，其中约 850 亿元指向芯片采购[1][4][8]。这些投入的直接动因是自有业务的调用量——企业披露当前算力利用率处于高位、服务器资源紧张，需要提前锁定硬件产能，腾讯 2025 年 AI 新产品投入约 180 亿元、2026 年计划至少翻倍[1]。
与芯片厂的合作形态在 2026 年趋于定型：一是云厂商自研芯片上云，用自有业务完成规模化验证；二是云厂商与芯片厂共建定制智算集群，围绕软件栈做联合调优；三是通过一体机把云端验证过的能力下沉到行业客户。三条路径的共同点，是芯片厂获得了规模化验证场景，云厂商获得了确定性供给——采购方、使用方与受益方三者合一，复购由业务量增长驱动，而非由预算周期驱动。
这一模式有明确边界：前提是自有场景能消化新增算力。 投入节奏跟着产品收入走，一旦场景增速放缓，重资产扩张会直接反噬利润表。判断这类主体的经营质量，应看 AI 产品收入与资本开支的比值是否稳定，而不是资本开支的绝对规模。
电信运营商： 优势在云网融合的存量资源。三大运营商将智算中心与算力网络作为发展方向，中国电信建设「2+3+7+X」公共智算资源池，中国移动依托「4+N+31+X」资源布局统筹智算中心布局，中国联通在「5+4+31+X」数据中心基础上打造智算集群[11][9]。网络时延控制、政企客户关系与属地化服务能力，是运营商区别于其他三类的禀赋；短板在云服务能力与软件生态的灵活性。运营商算力专项投入的预算稳定性高，但需求真伪同样要靠上架率与用算成效事后验证。
第三方算力服务商： 卖的是机房资产与大客户长协。国信证券口径下 TOP5 服务商合计份额超过 50%，万国数据以 17% 位列第一、机柜利用率 73.8%、预签约率 93.0%；润泽科技成熟算力中心上架率超过 90%，最大终端客户字节跳动贡献其约 57% 的营收[14]。中国信通院将第三方服务商的模式归纳为三类：批发型 IDC 代运维、零售与批发混合、AIDC 智算主力——第三类已实现从「出租机柜」向「出租算力及配套运维」的转变，单兆瓦价值量达到传统 IDC 的 3–5 倍[13]。头部的共同特征是「资源提前锁定＋深度绑定大客户＋定制批发」，在项目建设前期即签订长期合同；中小服务商在这三个环节上全面处于劣势。
两类主体的经营风险位置不同：运营商的风险在需求侧验证，第三方服务商的风险在客户集中度。 润泽科技单一客户占营收约 57%，说明头部第三方的高上架率本质是把经营风险从「找客户」转移为「绑大客户」；长协客户的续约与扩容意愿，是这类主体最需要持续核验的变量。
把四类主体的资源条件放到同一张表上比较，会发现长板长在不同的位置。政府主导与国资平台的优势在资源端——土地、能耗指标、电力接入与财政资金，是市场经营主体拿不到或拿不起的资源；电信运营商的优势在网络端——骨干网、时延控制与属地服务，使其在「云-边-端」一体化交付上不可替代；公有云厂商的优势在需求端——自有场景、开发者生态与按量计费体系；第三方算力服务商的优势在资产端——机房资产、电力容量与批发长协

items.title: Agent Tasks 10.71% Faster, Memory Footprint 21.60% Lower | Introducing Alibaba Cloud Linux 4
items.description: Agent Tasks 10.71% Faster, Memory Footprint 21.60% Lower | Introducing Alibaba Cloud Linux 4 This article introduces Alibaba Cloud Linux 4's system-level optimizations designed to accelerate AI Agent tasks and significantly reduce memory fo
items.detailText:
This article introduces Alibaba Cloud Linux 4's system-level optimizations designed to accelerate AI Agent tasks and significantly reduce memory footprint.
At scale, the cost of running agents goes beyond model calls. It also includes starting and running hundreds or thousands of isolated environments that execute tools and validate code. Alibaba Cloud Linux 4 (Alinux 4) now ships system-level optimizations built for Agent workloads , improving task turnaround from the operating system up, cutting the host memory footprint, and holding tail latency steadier over long runs.
Over the past year, Agents have taken on far more: answering questions, then calling tools, generating code, installing dependencies, running tests, and finally completing a workflow on their own. Compared with traditional online services, Agent workloads have one distinctive trait. They are not a single long-lived process ticking along steadily; they repeatedly create processes, allocate and free memory on interpreter heaps, and run compilation and test jobs.
Alibaba Cloud Linux 4 answers that shift by rethinking the relationship between Agents and the operating system. The OS is no longer just a general-purpose base that carries applications; it actively recognizes workloads characterized by short lifecycles, many processes, and high-frequency memory allocation. This release has a single core goal: run more Agent tasks, more reliably, on the same compute resources.
Alibaba Cloud Linux 4 introduces adaptive multi-size transparent huge pages (mTHP) for different working sets. Instead of committing to one page size, it picks the granularity that fits current available memory and workload characteristics: high efficiency while memory is plentiful, and a smooth step down when contiguous space runs short, avoiding the performance cliff that comes from dropping straight from huge pages to base pages.
The value here is not one more kernel parameter. It is that a trade-off among performance, memory, and stability that used to be tuned by hand now becomes a choice the system makes dynamically.
For an Agent platform, this kind of gain matters more than shaving a few milliseconds off a single request. Agents typically run multiple rounds of tool calling back to back, and waiting at any one step accumulates along the workflow. When dozens of sandboxes run at once, batch completion time directly shapes how fast the whole workflow turns over.
Memory is the other cost center for an Agent platform. Sandboxes are typically provisioned with fixed resource allocations for isolation and security, but their real working sets fluctuate constantly with tool calls. Run many sandboxes in parallel and memory fragmentation plus duplicated page-management overhead push host pressure higher still.

items.title: QwenWork × AgentBridge: Connecting Enterprise Data and Bringing Intelligent Analysis Within Reach
items.description: QwenWork × AgentBridge: Connecting Enterprise Data and Bringing Intelligent Analysis Within Reach This article introduces the QwenWork and AgentBridge suite for natural-language enterprise data analysis and verifiable reporting. Alibaba Clo
items.detailText:
This article introduces the QwenWork and AgentBridge suite for natural-language enterprise data analysis and verifiable reporting.
At the AI Real-Time Data Intelligence Forum of the 2026 Apsara Conference, QwenWork and AgentBridge officially released the Data Analysis Expert suite . Business users can ask a question in natural language and securely access multi-source enterprise data. They then receive an analyzed and verified report, ready for delivery.
One question in a weekly meeting often starts a series of preparation steps. It covers locating order data, checking logistics status, reviewing customer complaints, and confirming statistical definitions. The analysis results are then organized into a report. Enterprises have already accumulated large volumes of data. Business users still need to spend considerable time before they can turn that data into a decision and a document they can use.
Across execution, connectivity, evolution, and control, QwenWork links existing enterprise systems through connectors and MCP. It captures work experience as reusable Skills and Expert Suites, and it manages Agent usage with permissions and behavior auditing. For enterprises, these capabilities offer one further benefit. They let team members reuse working methods that are already proven, just as the widely quoted phrase puts it: "Context is All You Need".
This division of labor covers everyday office tasks such as ad-hoc data questions and data pulls, daily reports and briefings, weekly reviews, anomaly diagnosis, deep-dive analysis, and report analysis. Users can keep asking questions toward a business goal until they have a conclusion, a dashboard, or a report. This reduces the repetitive work of consolidating information between query tools and office software.
This demonstration uses customer refund analysis and retention to show how the solution works. Sample customer C10001 encountered a logistics delay and filed multiple complaints. The customer service lead needs to know what went wrong with the order and what the customer has already raised. The lead also needs to know what handling and retention recommendations can be proposed under the enterprise's current policy.
Once the data and analysis services are ready, business users can ask questions directly in QwenWork. For example: "How many times did the customer complain, and what was each complaint about?" They can also ask for further analysis of the refund causes and for retention recommendations based on the compensation rules.

items.title: AgentScope Durable: Running Enterprise Agents Continuously and Reliably
items.description: AgentScope Durable: Running Enterprise Agents Continuously and Reliably This article introduces AgentScope's Durable capabilities, enabling enterprise AI agents to reliably execute long-running tasks with automatic recovery and session pers
items.detailText:
This article introduces AgentScope's Durable capabilities, enabling enterprise AI agents to reliably execute long-running tasks with automatic recovery and session persistence.
A development agent receives a task: locate a fault, modify the code, run tests, and submit the results after obtaining approval. The model has completed its analysis, the tests need to run for twenty minutes, and approval may not arrive until the next day. In the meantime, the user closes the page, the service undergoes a rolling deployment, and the instance that initially executed the task is replaced.
This work should continue. Tests that have already started should be locatable, confirmed results should be reusable, and when approval arrives, an instance that meets the execution requirements should pick up the work. When the user opens the application again, they should still see the same task.
Figure 1: A task spans the user connection, the application, the agent process, and external execution systems. The orange markers identify continuity issues that must be addressed when a connection is lost, an instance is replaced, results are handed off, approval is pending, or the user returns.
These issues become common as agents take on long-term work. A development task involves analysis, modification, testing, and approval; a business operation may pass through multiple systems and wait for external feedback. When a task outlives the browser connection, service request, and execution instance, the application needs to maintain continuity across these boundaries.
The five issues in the figure point to the same requirement: persist the task's identity, execution progress, and conditions for continuation outside the process, and establish explicit recovery rules for them. The task still exists after the user goes offline; a compatible executor can take over after an instance is replaced; and when a tool completes or approval arrives, the system can locate the original task and continue the unfinished work.
This is what Durable means in this article: organizing an agent's execution process into state that can be durably saved, confirmed, and recovered, with continuation boundaries at native checkpoints, tool handoffs, waiting conditions, and similar points. Recovery continues from committed logical state, reuses confirmed results, and verifies unfinished external operations.
AgentScope's three core abstraction layers handle the reasoning loop, context management, and durable execution, respectively. Applications can combine these capabilities as needed.
Figure 2: ReActAgent provides the reasoning loop, HarnessAgent organizes context, and Durable manages the lifecycle of durable tasks.

items.title: 水面智能驾驶公司获数千万融资，加速近海无人作业平台落地｜硬氪首发
items.detailText:
累计交付客户近百家。
硬氪获悉，水面智能驾驶公司「仓潮科技」近日完成数千万元天使++轮融资，由兴业证券旗下兴证资本、上市公司高华科技联合投资，这是公司2026年完成的第三轮融资。资金将重点投向近海运维场景的数据化与产品落地、海洋物理AI技术研发、船级社认证及行业标准建设，同时推进近海世界模型的前沿探索。
本轮融资完成后，叠加此前种子轮、天使轮及天使+轮系列融资，仓潮科技累计融资规模近亿元。其中种子轮由连云港海洋基金出资，天使轮投资方包含云港集团、天汇资本、连云港金控集团，天使+轮投资方为海州湾发展集团。
仓潮科技2023年底成立，总部位于连云港，公司聚焦近海具身智能赛道，以“海洋物理AI”为技术底座，搭建了从底层算法到整船产品再到岸基控制的三层产品架构。最底层是自研的海洋物理AI体系，以智能航行AI大脑“海枢OceanHub”为核心；在此之上，衍生出澜、御、曜三大无人船整船系列，以及海枢船端智驾方案。这套架构让水上智驾能力可以适配不同船型、海域与作业场景。
团队由船舶工程、水下机器人、商业航天等前沿技术领域人士组成，核心成员兼具船舶设计与水上自动驾驶的交叉专业背景。创始人兼CEO程晨为河海大学博士，曾担任多地海事局外部技术顾问，深度参与多项国家重点研发项目。
近海海域水文、风浪、洋流、能见度条件动态多变，工况离散且不可复现，想要持续开展稳定、可控的海上实测并不容易。真实海洋工况下的有效样本获取成本高、采集周期长，缺少足量、覆盖各类极端工况的现场数据，模型很难持续迭代优化；而脱离常态化的海上实地验证，算法面对复杂海况的可靠性、容错能力也难以充分打磨。
“想要找到合适的海域，持续开展标准化实地测试，本身就是一件难度很高的事。”仓潮科技CEO程晨告诉硬氪。仓潮科技的探索，正是从破解这一行业痛点切入。种子轮阶段，依托连云港海洋基金的支持，公司进入初期测试海域开展多工况、长周期的实海试验，完成了早期的算法与系统验证工作。
程晨指出，海上智能算法的核心门槛，远不止是海域环境本身。更深层的考验，在于团队能否搭建起完整的“数据—模型—场景”闭环验证体系，持续沉淀海洋场景的专属数据；同时基于系统工程能力，在风浪、扰动等复杂多变的海洋工况里，保障无人航行装备稳定、可靠作业。
具体到底层算法的设计上，团队将船舶动力学模型与深度学习进行了深度融合，提出了“物理驱动神经网络控制算法”。通过将船舶的物理运动规律作为神经网络的“前置约束”，让模型在汲取数据的同时，进一步学习并理解船体在风浪、水流中该如何受力与响应。
这种“物理+数据”双轮驱动的模式，让仓潮科技的无人船即使面对复杂海况，也具备了更高精度的机动控制与轨迹追踪能力。
在此基础上，仓潮科技同步搭建面向近海的领域世界模型。和陆地道路环境不同，海面没有固定车道、标志物会随潮汐和水流持续变化，浮标、通航船舶、水下障碍物的位置都具备动态属性，静态电子海图已经不足以支撑实时航行决策。
近海世界模型的价值，就是把静态海图升级为能够感知、推演环境变化的动态环境底座。硬氪了解到，依托连云港周边数百公里水域的全域环境重建及常态化实海测试，仓潮科技已将实时海况数据、动态障碍物信息与电子海图融合，训练出面向垂直场景的端到端模型。该模型能够预判水流、风浪对船体运动的影响，推演周边船舶的航行意图，并在决策链路前端识别潜在风险。
进入产业化环节，海洋经济版图中，海上执法、海洋测绘与海上新能源运维是三个具备明确需求增量的场景。以海上光伏与风电为例，随着大规模基础设施建设逐步铺开，日常运维、海缆监测、海床勘测、无人机清洗等作业需求正在快速增长。传统有人船作业模式面临人力成本高、作业窗口受海况限制、人员安全风险大等痛点，无人化与自主化的替代空间正在打开。
在仓潮科技团队看来，如果智能无人船仅停留在“能在水面上按预定路线跑起来”，它依然只是一个运载工具，无法真正切入上述场景的核心痛点。
海上具身智能的真正门槛，在于解决具体的作业问题。为此，仓潮科技构建了一套异构协同作业系统，无人船作为中枢平台，负责自动驾驶与任务规划；无人机作为空中视角与轻量化载荷载体；水下机器人则承担水下作业任务。三者协同，覆盖从海面到水下的全维度监控与运维需求。
落到商业模式上，仓潮科技形成了两条并行的产品线。一条是标准化智驾盒子，面向存量船舶的智能化改造，可适配冲锋舟、救援艇、水上靶船等场景，安装过程控制在半小时到一小时，目前已实现批量化交付；另一条是自持无人船产品线，聚焦海上巡逻、光伏运维、风电运维等场景，提供从船体到智驾系统的完整解决方案。
目前，仓潮科技累计交付客户近百家，覆盖海事系统、海警系统、边防系统等政府单位，以及涉港单位和多家海上风电开发商，并与中国船级社、河海大学、江苏科技大学、上海大学等高校及科研机构合作，产品逐步进入稳定化使用阶段。
硬氪：如果单看航行避障算法，海上场景的复杂度确实低于城市道路的车载自动驾驶。目前，制约海上智驾大规模产业化的核心工程瓶颈主要在哪些环节？
程晨： 如果把问题仅仅局限在“船舶能不能在水面上按预定路线避障航行”，那它的算法复杂度和算力需求，确实低于车载自动驾驶。船舶的运动自由度有限，水面障碍物的种类和城市道路里突发的人车混流相比，也相对可控。但这是一个剥离了真实作业环境的理想视角。
第一层，是实海数据闭环的获取门槛。在陆地，车企可以大规模铺测试车上路，通过高频次的路测快速驱动算法迭代。但在近海和内河，由于海事监管极其严格，你不仅需要合规的船舶，还需要获批的专属海域才能进行实海测试。风浪、潮汐、涌流、泥沙、能见度这些动态工况，其样本获取成本极高。如果没有稳定的测试海域做支撑，你就很难积累出完备的极端工况数据集。这不是纯写代码能解决的问题，而是海洋场景特有的工程前置条件。
第二层，也是真正拉开差距的地方，航行智能与行业深层业务逻辑的耦合。 海事巡逻执法、海上光伏风电运维、海床测绘，每一个垂直领域背后，都有几十年沉淀下来的作业规范、处置流程和行业标准。真正的难点是把这些非标的行业知识图谱，与智驾决策层深度融合，把船长、专家的作业经验，转化为机器能听懂、能执行的任务逻辑。
让船在海上跑起来，行业内不少团队都能实现。但让船真正理解风电运维的作业逻辑、懂海事执法的处置规范，这需要团队不仅得懂船舶动力学和AI模型，还得深度浸泡在一线的海洋工程现场。这是一种典型的跨学科系统工程，也是我们一直死磕的底层壁垒。
硬氪：从产业现实来看，高阶水面智驾的商业化节奏会如何演进？仓潮为何采取L2标准化改造与L3/L4高阶系统并行的产品路线，背后逻辑是什么？
程晨： 技术研发可以适度走在产业需求之前，但商业化落地必须匹配行业的政策、合规与客户的真实付费意愿。

items.detailText:
Vercel
A monthly overview of things you need to know as an architect or aspiring architect.
Facilitating the Spread of Knowledge and Innovation in Professional Software Development
Unlock the full InfoQ experience by logging in! Stay updated with your favorite authors and topics, engage with content, and download exclusive resources.
In this episode, Christopher "CRob" Robinson, CTO of OpenSSF, Akrites, and chief security architect of the Linux Foundation, explores the state of software supply chain security amid multiple security incidents and explains how tools like Scorecard, the Security Baseline framework, and SLSA help harden software.
Saranya Vedagiri explains how to design resilient, low-latency distributed APIs under 100ms. Drawing on practical scale at eBay, she discusses hop-by-hop latency budgets, async fanout tradeoffs, thread pool sizing, caching, and circuit breakers. Learn actionable strategies to eliminate tail-latency bottlenecks and establish performance-first engineering practices.
Rachel Shalom explains how Dell solved enterprise RAG retrieval failures on internal terminology by fine-tuning open-source embedding models. She discusses data prep with hard negatives, distributed InfoNCE loss training on H100 GPUs, automated hyperparameter tuning, and production evaluation using LLM-as-a-judge.
Laura Savino discusses the psychological friction of AI adoption for senior engineers & architects. She explains how shifting from static expertise to learning in public lowers anxiety, accelerates tooling fluency, and prevents burnout. Leaders will discover actionable strategies to support their teams, debunk tech zealotry, and foster an adaptive engineering culture that thrives during upheaval.
The panelists explore how engineering teams adapt delivery architectures, pipelines, security, and governance for AI-assisted development. They share practical strategies for verifying AI-generated code, solving testing and deployment bottlenecks, maintaining human oversight, and measuring AI’s true impact on software velocity, quality, reliability, and operational cost.

items.title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
items.detailText:
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.
We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.
The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.
Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:
Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made generally available on September 30.
Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.
Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.
Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation. Our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.
